summary: V2 upgrade testing — Databento OI integration + 2D grid heatmap + Swing mode + Contract Drilldown + Flowseeker SSE. All 8 new backend pytest tests + all 9 prior tests pass (17/17). Frontend renders grid with KING/FLR/CEIL/GATE/AIR tags, teal/purple/yellow-green cells, spot row inline. View toggle (Grid<->Bars), mode toggle (Day<->Swing), Trinity 3-panel, Flowseeker SSE lifecycle, and Drilldown modal (open via cell click, close via close button + click-outside, shows delta/gamma/gex/oi_source=databento) all working. Grid response uses integer-string strike keys (e.g. '739' not '739.0'). data_source = 'databento+yfinance' on all heatmap responses; databento_oi Mongo collection has cached snapshots.

issues: Clicking an empty grid cell (strike+expiry with no OI for that pair) still opens the modal showing '0 contracts'. Not a bug — the underlying data truly has no contract — but UX would be cleaner if empty cells were non-clickable or showed a 'no contracts at this strike/expiry' message.
With swing mode (±25% band) on dense tickers, the strike list can exceed 200 rows. Center column becomes very tall. Consider virtualization or magMin-based row filtering for swing mode.

When market is closed / very low trade flow, the stream lifecycle goes idle -> ready -> ended within ~5s and the Stop button disappears. This is expected (no live trades after hours) but a brief status hint like 'stream ended — market closed?' would help users.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py L188-194 fetch_spot_and_chains_merged: `iv_by_expiry.setdefault(...).append(...) if False else None` is dead code (the `if False` short-circuits). The IV averaging then uses a running pairwise mean which is mathematically biased (each new sample halves the weight of all prior). Fix: collect IVs into a list and compute true arithmetic mean, e.g. `iv_avg_by_expiry[e] = sum(ivs)/len(ivs)`.
server.py contract_drilldown sends rows even when 0 results — frontend opens a useless empty modal. Either return 404 when count==0 or surface a clearer 'no contracts' empty state on the client.

databento_provider.py L201 `if dry_run or not DBN_KEY: return` — when DBN_KEY is empty, /api/flow SSE sends no error event before EOF, so the UI silently shows 'ended' with no explanation. Suggest queueing an `{_error: 'Databento key missing'}` instead.

server.py compute_gex_grid strike key normalization: `str(int(x)) if float(x).is_integer() else str(x)` is correct for whole numbers but '739.5' will stringify to '739.5' (good); however some tickers (e.g. SPX) may have strikes like 5000.0 — works fine. Edge case: negative-strike anomalies (shouldn't exist) would produce '-739' which is consistent.

server.py /api/flow uses `live.block_for_close(timeout=300)` inside asyncio.to_thread — the stop_event is checked only inside cb. If callbacks aren't fired (no trades after hours), the thread blocks for 5 min holding the connection. Consider polling stop_event in a wrapper, or pass max_seconds down to limit the live timeout.

Drilldown frontend sends both expiry+strike via query params; backend correctly filters. But strike is sent as JavaScript number — for half-strikes the URL will be '740.5' and backend parses to float — OK.
seed_data_creation: Mongo `databento_oi` collection pre-warmed with SPY/QQQ/SPXW OI snapshots from heatmap calls; `snapshots` collection accumulates per-call snapshots for velocity/rolling.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests: test_heatseeker.py (v1) + test_heatseeker_v2.py (v2 grid/swing/drilldown/databento). Run with `REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=<public-url> pytest /app/backend/tests/ -v`. Databento OI fetch is ~10-30s on cold cache per ticker; tests use 120-240s timeouts. Drilldown can take 10-15s on first call (yfinance+databento merge). Flowseeker streams cost real money — DO NOT leave running >20s in tests. After-hours flow streams end almost immediately with 0 trades, this is normal.
